key_findings: AQLM (Extreme Compression of Large Language Models via Additive Quantization) is the state-of-the-art method for 2-3 bit LLM compression, published at ICML 2024 (arXiv:2401.06118)

Vector quantization outperforms scalar quantization at ultra-low bitrates (below 3-bit) because it preserves weight correlations and learns data-dependent codebooks, achieving better rate-distortion tradeoffs
AQLM's additive decomposition (summing multiple codebook entries) is more flexible than product quantization and enables hierarchical error correction across codebooks
Joint optimization of codebooks and weight assignments is crucial - alternating assignment and centroid updates (similar to LBG algorithm) converges to good local minima
AQLM achieves only +1.46 perplexity increase on Llama 2 7B at 2-bit vs +2.75 for previous methods (29% better), and scales exceptionally well to larger models (+0.11 on 70B)
Custom per-layer quantization (adaptive bitrate allocation) can improve quality by 0.5-1% over uniform quantization by accounting for layer-specific importance and distribution differences
AQLM is actively maintained (GitHub: Vahe1994/AQLM, v1.1.7 April 2025) with official implementations for GPU/CPU inference and integration into HuggingFace Transformers and PEFT
Layer-aware quantization outperforms blackbox methods because different layers have different sensitivity - embedding/early layers need more bits while later layers can use fewer bits
Mathematical foundation: AQLM represents weights as W ≈ ∑(m=1 to M) C_m b_m where C_m are learned codebooks and b_m are one-hot code vectors
For 1-bit to 32-bit integration: use unified framework with modular codebook learning - same algorithm with varying M (number of codebooks) and B (bits per codebook)

vector_quantization_advantage.principle: Rate-distortion theory shows VQ can achieve lower distortion than scalar quantization at very low bitrates
vector_quantization_advantage.reason: VQ preserves weight correlations and learns data-dependent codebooks, while scalar quantization treats each weight independently
vector_quantization_advantage.bitrate_region: Below 3 bits per parameter, VQ advantage becomes dominant
vector_quantization_advantage.key_equation: D(R) for VQ < D(R) for scalar quantization when R < H(X)

aqlm_core_equation.description: Weight reconstruction as sum of codebook vectors

components.b_m: one-hot code vector selecting entry from C_m

optimized_loss_form.equation: L = ||WX||²_2 - 2∑_m ⟨W, C_m b_m⟩_{XX^T} + ∑_{i,j} ⟨C_i b_i, C_j b_j⟩_{XX^T}
optimized_loss_form.precomputable: Frobenius inner products with XX^T for fast optimization

mathematical_foundations.key_insight: Additive decomposition allows codebooks to specialize - each captures different aspects of weight variation, enabling hierarchical error correction superior to single VQ

algorithm_three_phase_process.name: Discrete Code Optimization
algorithm_three_phase_process.description: Beam search to find optimal one-hot codes b_m using Markov Random Field
algorithm_three_phase_process.solves: Discrete assignment problem with unary and pairwise potentials

algorithm_three_phase_process.name: Codebook Update
algorithm_three_phase_process.description: Optimize continuous codebook vectors C_m via Adam optimizer
algorithm_three_phase_process.objective: Minimize ||WX - W_hat X||²_2 with respect to C_m

algorithm_three_phase_process.name: Fine-tuning
algorithm_three_phase_process.description: After all layers quantized, fine-tune all parameters jointly
algorithm_three_phase_process.benefit: Accounts for inter-layer interactions and backpropagates errors through codebook representation

why_custom_quantization_outperforms.problem_with_uniform: Single pre-trained method across all layers assumes uniform sensitivity, but layer importance varies dramatically
layer_differences: Embedding layers: very sensitive, need 4+ bits
Early transformer layers: important for feature extraction, need 2-3 bits
Middle layers: moderate importance, can use 2-bit
Late layers: redundant heads possible, can use 1.5-bit
why_custom_quantization_outperforms.distribution_variation: Weight distributions differ per layer (embedding weights much smaller, MLP more compressible)
why_custom_quantization_outperforms.solution: Allocate bits based on Fisher information or Hessian diagonal - more important layers get more bits
why_custom_quantization_outperforms.expected_improvement: 0.5-1% better perplexity at same average bitrate vs blackbox uniform quantization

phase_4_framework_integration: CUDA kernels for fast codebook lookups

unified_framework_for_1_to_32_bit.concept: Single framework supporting all bitrates via modular codebook learning
unified_framework_for_1_to_32_bit.approach: Same AQLM algorithm, vary M (number of codebooks) and B (bits per codebook)

insights: Vector quantization fundamentally outperforms scalar quantization at ultra-low bitrates because it preserves spatial correlations between weights and learns data-dependent codebooks. AQLM's key innovation is the additive decomposition (summing multiple codebooks rather than concatenating), which provides finer quantization granularity and enables hierarchical error correction. The joint optimization of codebooks and assignments, alternating between discrete code selection (via MRF) and continuous codebook learning (via gradient descent), is critical - this mirrors the classical LBG algorithm but applied to the LLM compression problem. Your custom quantization approach outperforms blackbox methods because layer-specific importance varies dramatically: embeddings need high precision while later layers can be heavily compressed. The mathematical foundation from rate-distortion theory explains why AQLM achieves near-lossless 2-bit compression (only +1.46 perplexity on Llama 7B vs +2.75 for prior methods) - the additive structure lets each codebook specialize in capturing different aspects of the weight distribution. For Project-Tensor integration, a unified framework with modular codebook learning can support all bitrates from 1-bit to 32-bit by simply adjusting the number of codebooks and bits per codebook.
